headlines.title: Emergency crews respond to hazardous materials incident in San Francisco
headlines.description: Emergency crews are responding to a hazardous materials incident Friday in San Francisco. The San Francisco Fire Department said the incident involves muriatic acid and chlorine at the Presidio Golf and Concordia Golf Course. At least one person was taken to a hospital due to the incident. Hazardous materials units and fire crews are on scene investigating. Residents and the public should avoid the area. No other information was immediately available. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: 8 arrested in San Jose shooting that killed a man, injured another
headlines.description: San Jose police Friday announced the arrests of eight people for their alleged involvement in a June shooting that killed a man and injured another. The suspects were arrested for their alleged parts in a shooting on June 28 near the intersection of North Market and West Santa Clara streets. One man, 24-year-old Anthony Contreras, died at the scene and another was taken to a hospital and listed in stable condition. The suspects were identified by police officials as Izaiah Hernandez, 18, Ezequiel Mercado, 20, Jaden Diaz-Mejia, 18, Fabian Diaz-Gomez, 18, and Johnny Picazo, 36, who were all booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of murder, along with an unnamed 17-year-old suspect. Additionally, Sabastian Saldana, 34, and Nevaeh Luna-Rosales, 18, were booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of crimes related to being accessories after the fact, according to police. The motive and circumstances surrounding the shooting are still under investigation. It was the city’s 13th homicide of 2026.

headlines.title: Suspect arrested in San Jose deadly shooting
headlines.description: An arrest has been made in the fatal shooting of a man in San Jose, police announced Friday. The shooting, which occurred Wednesday night on Stockton Avenue near Taylor Street, marked San Jose’s 18th homicide of the year. San Jose resident Andre Duckett was arrested in connection with the shooting on Thursday in Oakland, police said. Duckett, 39, was identified as a suspect after San Jose police detectives used license plate readers to track a suspect vehicle. He was booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of murder, police said. A motive and the shooting are still under investigation, according to police. Anyone with information can contact Detective Sgt. Barragan at 4106@sanjoseca.gov or Detective Harrington at 4365@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-5283. headlines.title: Richmond officer shot by woman while responding to behavioral health crisis call
headlines.description: A Richmond police officer was seriously injured after being shot while responding to a behavioral health crisis call Thursday evening, police said. Contra Costa County’s behavioral health crisis response team was called to conduct a mental health check on a person in the 2200 block of Key Boulevard shortly after 6:30 p.m. Richmond police were asked to assist because of potential safety concerns, according to authorities. Police said the first officer to arrive at the home was struck by gunfire almost immediately. The officer was taken to a hospital in serious condition but is expected to survive. Following the shooting, a female suspect barricaded herself inside the home and continued firing multiple rounds from within, police said. According to the police chief, bullets struck neighboring homes, cars and a Richmond police patrol vehicle. No residents or additional personnel were injured. Multiple agencies responded to the scene, including SWAT teams, the Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office and crisis negotiators. Police eventually used chemical agents, and the suspect came out of the home and was taken into custody. The officer was the only person injured during the incident. The investigation remains ongoing.
headlines.source: Victoria Meza and Ginger Conejero Saab

headlines.title: Bicyclist dies after collision in San Jose
headlines.description: A bicyclist was killed in a collision early Friday morning in San Jose, police said. Officers responded at about 4:20 a.m. to the intersection of Trimble Road and North First Street for a collision involving a vehicle and a bicyclist. A preliminary investigation found that a man driving a gray 2024 Toyota Corolla was traveling westbound on Trimble Road through a green light when he struck a bicyclist traveling northbound on North First Street in the crosswalk, according to police. When officers arrived, they found an adult man unconscious and not breathing. He was pronounced dead at the scene, according to police. The driver remained at the scene and cooperated with investigators, according to police. Drugs and alcohol do not appear to have been factors in the collision, police said. The death marks San Jose’s 33rd fatal collision and 33rd traffic-related death of 2026. The investigation remains ongoing.

headlines.title: Caldecott Tunnel to get $267 million in state and federal help with upgrades
headlines.description: State leaders have announced a slew of funding going towards transportation infrastructure across the state, and that includes funding for major upgrades to the East Bay’s Caldecott Tunnel. These changes would fund the ventilation project at the tunnel as well as make improvements to pavement, drainage, and lighting. Gov. Gavin Newsom announced that the state is investing a total of $2.7 billion in more than 150 transportation projects across the state, using $1.6 billion in federal funding and $542 million from state funding. In Newsom’s announcement about these statewide projects, the Caldecott Tunnel was at the top of the list. The update from his office said $267 million of that funding will go towards rehabilitating and upgrading the ventilation systems on three of the four bores at the Caldecott Tunnel. The announcement says this project will replace the tunnel’s structural pavement, upgrade drainage, and improve electrical systems to LED lighting. This provides funding for a ventilation project Caltrans has already been working towards. Caltrans said they do not have a date scheduled yet for when the major work will begin on this project. headlines.title: Man found dead at Vallejo park
headlines.description: A man was found deceased in a Vallejo park earlier this week, police said Friday. The body was discovered “in or near” Lake Chabot around 4 p.m. Tuesday, according to the Vallejo Police Department. The man has not been identified. His death is currently under investigation by the Solano County Coroner’s Office.

headlines.title: Stanford community honors late soccer player Katie Meyer
headlines.description: It was a historic and emotional Thursday night at Stanford, as the women’s soccer team retired number 19: the number worn by star goalkeeper Katie Meyer, who died by suicide in 2022. Meyer’s parents, Gina and Steve, walked to midfield to a standing ovation, surrounded by the team, coaches and fans who came to honor their daughter. “It warms my heart, breaks my heart, warms my heart, the whole thing,” Steve Meyer said. “We used to walk in through those doors. I see it in my eyes right now, so it’s tough. She’d be right over there warming up,” Katie Meyer was a captain for Stanford. In the 2019 national championship game, she made two critical saves to help Stanford beat North Carolina. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or chat live at 988lifeline.org. You can also visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional support. headlines.title: Pittsburg officer, suspect shot after altercation during booking process
headlines.description: A police officer and a suspect hospitalized after being shot during an altercation at the Pittsburg police station Thursday, according to the police department. Police said officers arrested a 31-year-old man and took him to the police station for booking. While booking, authorities said a physical altercation occurred between the suspect and an officer, during which a firearm was discharged, striking the officer and the suspect. The officer was taken to John Muir Medical Center in Walnut Creek in serious but stable condition. The suspect was also hospitalized and was in stable condition, according to police. Police have not said whose firearm was discharged or provided additional details about what led up to the struggle. The shooting remains under investigation.

headlines.title: 2 hospitalized after shots fired from vehicle in Suisun City
headlines.description: Two people were shot in a car in Suisun City on Thursday evening, according to police. Around 7:10 p.m. Thursday, two individuals were found suffering from gunshot wounds in their car near the 1300 block of Blossom Avenue. Suisun City police said that several rounds had been fired from a car driving alongside the two victims. Both were taken to a hospital and sustained non-life-threatening injuries. The shooting follows a separate case in Suisun City on Monday around 10:20 p.m. in which police said suspects fired several rounds into an apartment building in the 600 block of Civic Center Boulevard. Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact the Suisun City Police Department Investigations Unit at 707-421-7373. Reports can be anonymous.

headlines.title: Multiple businesses burglarized in Danville
headlines.description: At least 11 businesses in Danville were burglarized early Tuesday morning, leaving owners on edge. Xu Xia, a worker at Hashiya Sushi, came to work Tuesday morning to find the newly opened sushi restaurant had been burglarized. Surveillance video shows three men dressed in hoodies smashing through the front door and going straight to the cash register which fortunately was nearly empty. The burglars smashed into a neighboring Vietnamese restaurant, also going straight for the cash. In the same shopping center, they smashed their way into a nail salon, also Asian owned. “I think they probably thought they probably thought Asians had more cash in the store,so that’s why they target mostly Asian restaurants,” Xia said. Across the street, three more businesses were hit: a Thai restaurant, a Greek restaurant and another sushi spot. On the other side of town, burglars targeted five more businesses, including a hair salon. Stylist Connie Palomino says, surprisingly, the only thing they took was one of the surveillance cameras and some snacks. She speculates all the break-ins worked up an appetite. The burglars also loaded up with liquor at Los Panchos Mexican Restaurant and tried to break the cash register. Thieves also hit a kebab restaurant, a Domino’s and an Indian eatery. The burglary spree has business owners on edge. Many are asking for more police protection. NBC Bay Area reached out to Danville police but has not heard back.

headlines.title: Morgan Hill summer camp counselor accused of sexually assaulting 10-year-old girls
headlines.description: A Gilroy man accused of sexually assaulting three 10-year-old girls while working as a summer camp counselor is scheduled to be arraigned Friday. Anthony Joseph Ramon faces five counts of felony child molestation for attacks the district attorney claims took place in June at a Morgan Hill swim center. The 25-year-old Ramon was arrested three different times for each alleged assault. Prosecutors not only want him to be held accountable, but also want to know why Ramon was allowed to post bail after each arrest. Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen intends to ask the judge to hold Ramon on no bail during Friday’s formal arraignment on multiple assaults. “Bail should always be about protecting public safety,” Rosen said in a statement. “The idea that a person suspected of sexually abusing multiple children should get the same chance at freedom as a person accused of mail fraud or some other non-violent crime is wrong, and dangerous.” Santa Clara County Aug 31 Gilroy Aug 16 Legal analyst Steven Clark said Ramon was allowed to post bail because each arrest occurred separately. “Now that the cases will be consolidated in one place, that’s where I think the court will the say ‘He’s now facing a life sentence and no bail is allowed,'” Clark said. “But for the defense, they’re gonna say that he has made his court appearance that he posted enough bail to secure both his appearances. He’s not a flight risk and he is presumed innocent.” Ramon was a counselor for YMCA Silicon Valley when he worked a school summer camp field trip to the Morgan Hill Aquatic Center. In the weeks following, police arrested Ramon repeatedly after three individual 10-year-old girls came forward — one by one — claiming he molested them in the pool. Police said the case is an active investigation and are still looking for more possible victims.
